## 1.  Textual Features That Tend to Make AI‑Generated Writing Detectable

| Feature | Why it’s a red flag | Typical AI signature |
|---------|--------------------|----------------------|
| **Over‑polished, uniform style** | Human prose usually contains subtle variations in tone, rhythm, and word choice. | AI models are trained on large corpora and often produce a “mid‑point” style that feels smooth but lacks idiosyncratic quirks. |
| **Repetitive phrasing or sentence structures** | Humans tend to vary sentence length and structure; AI can fall into patterns (e.g., “In addition, …” or “Furthermore, …”). | Repeated use of the same transition words or clause patterns. |
| **Excessive use of generic or cliché phrases** | AI relies on high‑frequency n‑grams; it may over‑use common academic tropes (“in this study,” “the results indicate,” “it is evident that”). | Phrases that appear in many training documents, leading to a “generic” feel. |
| **Unnatural precision or over‑confidence** | AI can produce statements that sound definitive even when evidence is weak or absent. | “It is clear that X” or “The data conclusively prove Y” without proper citation or nuance. |
| **Inconsistent depth or abrupt topic jumps** | Human writers usually develop ideas gradually; AI may switch topics or depth abruptly because it is following a prompt rather than a coherent narrative. | Sudden shift from a detailed explanation to a high‑level summary without transition. |
| **Over‑use of passive voice** | Many AI models default to passive constructions because they are common in academic corpora. | “The experiment was conducted” repeated many times. |
| **Lack of personal voice or first‑person perspective** | Human authors often embed their own perspective, especially in reflective or methodological sections. | Entirely third‑person, impersonal tone. |
| **Unusual word choice or rare collocations** | AI may combine words that are statistically plausible but rarely used together by humans. | “The paradigm of the methodology” instead of “the methodological paradigm.” |
| **Inconsistent formatting or citation style** | AI may copy citation patterns from training data but fail to maintain consistency across the document. | Mixed APA/MLA styles, inconsistent use of italics or quotation marks.
